findings.observed_fact: Clearing the room field left No room found visible; submitting the empty query returned to the initial state.
findings.hypothesis: A user may read the stale result as belonging to the empty field. No participant confusion has been measured.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status: distinguish the submitted query from the editable query.
findings.suggestion: Evaluate explicit submitted-query context or clearing the result when the input is cleared.
requires_validation: Confirm intended query semantics
Observe real users performing clear-and-retry

findings.observed_fact: One click on a green available time-slot card produced no visible change.
findings.hypothesis: Card styling may imply selectable details to some users; this is not evidence of a broken booking feature.
findings.principle: Affordance and feedback: appearance should communicate whether the item is informational or actionable.
findings.suggestion: If informational, evaluate a clearly labelled availability table; if actionable, verify expected action and feedback first.
requires_validation: Test a second slot with reliable hit target
Confirm product intent
Ask real participants what they expect

findings.observed_fact: Preview loaded a webpage near its top; a downward scroll revealed Room: AG206 and its photographs. Closing Preview retained the Room filter.
findings.hypothesis: Unrelated page header/intro may add effort before users reach the selected room; actual user cost is unmeasured.
findings.principle: Match between system and user goal; continuity of context on return.
findings.suggestion: Evaluate a direct room-content anchor while retaining room/date/filter context on return.
requires_validation: Repeat to see whether initial scroll position is stable
Verify room content below the photograph
Measure with real participants

findings.observed_fact: After Sun selection a screenshot briefly showed the old 29-Sep result; a later observation showed 04-Oct with No available room, without another Search click.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status during asynchronous updates.
findings.suggestion: Represent both the observed transition and settled state; do not label the transient mismatch as a confirmed defect.
requires_validation: Repeat the change with captured loading feedback before drawing latency or usability conclusions

additional_observations.observed_fact: On resume the date strip says Today02-Oct while retained AG206 results still say30-Sep (Today). Query refresh, actual result-date data and the cause were not tested.

findings.observed_fact: A text link in the weather article opens the official Academic Registry website in an embedded browser, with a cookie notice.
findings.hypothesis: The transition may require users to recognise a different website context; no participant confusion has been observed.
findings.principle: Consistency and visibility of system status across an embedded web handoff.
findings.suggestion: Preserve a clear webpage context and verify a reliable close/return path in the prototype.
requires_validation: Inspect the actual close feedback and cookie controls
Observe real users locating the policy and returning

findings.observed_fact: Hero expand opens an image overlay; X restores the weather article.
findings.principle: User control and freedom through a reversible overlay.
findings.suggestion: Reproduce both expand and close; a static enlarged image does not reproduce this flow.
requires_validation: Inspect any other image gestures separately

findings.observed_fact: Hero appears above previously visible text and moves the here link downward. Old-position attempt stays on article; newly located link opens chatbot.
findings.hypothesis: A reader preparing to activate the link may need to locate it again; no human error rate or task cost measured.
findings.principle: Stable positioning and error prevention during asynchronous content loading.
findings.suggestion: Compare reserved hero space/loading placeholder while preserving image expansion and verified return paths.
requires_validation: Continuous cold/warm loading capture
Real user link-targeting task
Phone viewport comparison

findings.observed_fact: Settings third row shows a switch-like control without visible label; current AX also lacks description. No toggle attempted.
findings.hypothesis: Users may not be able to predict what changing this control does; human impact and intended function are unverified.
findings.principle: Recognition rather than recall and understandable control meaning.
findings.suggestion: Verify intended function and platform behavior before adding a visible label and matching accessibility name.
requires_validation: Reopen and compare real iPhone
Confirm intended setting function without blind toggling
Observe users interpreting the control

findings.observed_fact: In Mac AX, September 26 date-cell name is Sunday while visual selected date says Saturday; Thursday labels also include Thursdya spelling.
findings.hypothesis: May affect assistive reading of dates; no VoiceOver or participant test performed.
findings.principle: Accessible names should convey the same date meaning as visual labels.
findings.suggestion: Reproduce on target platform and inspect accessible date names before concluding user impact.
requires_validation: Independent AX replication
Real iOS VoiceOver date navigation
Confirm visual calendar remains correct

additional_observations.observed_fact: Oct2 selected-day AX says no entries while a Class card is visible. Oct3 in Saturday column is called Sunday by AX; source text is preserved in safe subsets. VoiceOver behavior and user impact remain untested.

Oct3 Payment date cell AX says Today Sunday3October selected, while visible Saturday column and selected title say Saturday,October3. Independently observed on current Mac; VoiceOver/iPhone impact untested.

findings.observed_fact: After rightward category-strip drag, All/Campus/Study become visible while Job Board content and AX-selected Job remain; the selected Job category is outside visible strip. Actual All selection occurs only at the next click.
findings.hypothesis: A user who scrolls category tabs may lose the visible cue identifying the current filter. No human confusion or error rate has been measured.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status: active filtering context should remain identifiable while navigation options move.
findings.suggestion: Compare keeping a visible current-category label or indicator while allowing independent horizontal category navigation; preserve actual existing behavior in original-app reconstruction.
requires_validation: Ask participants to identify current category after dragging tabs
Repeat on real iPhone with native touch
Compare whether existing content already identifies category sufficiently
Check reverse drag, repeated selection and category scroll retention

findings.observed_fact: Native amount eye buttons expose private-use glyphs eye-slash/eye in Mac AX without a descriptive Show/Hide amount name; clicking changes visible masked/unmasked state and reverse restores it. Actual amounts excluded.
findings.hypothesis: People using assistive navigation may have difficulty predicting or identifying amount disclosure from glyph-only names. No iOS VoiceOver or human error evidence yet.
findings.principle: Understandable control meaning, state visibility and accessible naming.
findings.suggestion: Verify on iPhone/VoiceOver; evaluate descriptive Show/Hide outstanding amount names and announced visibility state. Prototype still reconstructs observed behavior, not candidate fix.
requires_validation: iPhone VoiceOver name/state readout
People interpreting eye icon and amount privacy
Language/platform differences
